rationale: The retrospective Parkinson cohort measured facial tremor in the off-medication examination and evaluated clinical determinants and progression. The comparison groups differ by facial tremor status, without fig intake or a dietary exposure estimate.

The observational study measures wrist and elbow motion in Parkinson participants without overt clinical tremor and compares it with physiologic tremor in controls. Joint displacement and frequency have no raw-fig contrast.

Wearable gait measures distinguish early Parkinson disease from essential tremor and are compared with MDS-UPDRS motor subscores. The measured feature is gait performance, with no fig dietary assignment or fig-linked rest-tremor estimate.

The study compares automated MRI brain volumetry in refractory essential tremor and tremor-dominant Parkinson disease. Structural differences and clinical grouping have no raw-fig exposure or dietary tremor comparison.

Patients with medication-refractory Parkinson tremor receive targeted focused ultrasound ablation of the ventral intermediate thalamus or subthalamic nucleus. The exposure is selected surgery, with no fig assignment or dietary effect.

The four-year Parkinson cohort measures upper-limb rest tremor and separately assesses re-emergent, postural and kinetic tremor. Its observed clinical trajectories supply no fig exposure measure or dietary symptom contrast.

The focused ultrasound thalamotomy study reports blinded upper-limb rest-tremor assessments after a unilateral procedure. The before-and-after contrast concerns ablation and does not measure raw-fig intake.

Intraoperative electrophysiology compares subthalamic activity in Parkinson disease and essential tremor during deep-brain stimulation surgery. Beta-frequency activity by diagnosis does not supply a fig or food effect on rest tremor.

The case relates mixed tremor and worsening Parkinson symptoms to concurrent vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia and midbrain compression, with subsequent medication adjustment. It observes no fig exposure or related resting-tremor change.

Wavelet analysis quantifies wrist-sensor tremor signals from free-living Parkinson recordings. Its device measures capture fluctuation and correlate with clinical assessments without a fig exposure or diet comparison.

The paper models adaptive feedback control of postural and rest tremor through deep-brain stimulation. Its control analysis tests electrical stimulation parameters without an assigned fig diet or patient food contrast.

The experiment crosses positive, negative and neutral verbal expectations in people with implanted deep-brain stimulation, recording rest tremor under medication conditions. The placebo and nocebo manipulations are verbal, with no fig exposure.

The experiment records hand tremor and subthalamic local-field potentials as stimulation voltage changes in Parkinson disease. Tremor and gamma-power responses concern deep-brain stimulation without any food contrast.
An inertial finger sensor records rest, postural and kinetic tasks in Parkinson disease and essential tremor. Temporal fluctuation is used to discriminate diagnoses, with no raw-fig exposure.

The physiology study records electromyography across muscles in a planar postural task. Its synchronization and tremor-intensity comparison during the task has no dietary exposure or fig-related resting-tremor result.

The pilot evaluates single-trajectory deep-brain stimulation of the dentato-rubro-thalamic tract and subthalamic nucleus. Its reported clinical changes follow implantation and stimulation, without a fig comparison.

The study evaluates spectral algorithms for detecting tremor segments in accelerometer recordings against clinical classification. The diagnostic comparison supplies no fig intake or food-related resting-tremor change.
The short-term imaging study compares resting-state regional homogeneity and clinical tremor before and after unilateral thalamotomy. The exposure is surgery without raw-fig assignment.

The NEDICES analysis compares education and incident dementia across prevalent or future essential tremor and control groups. Its outcome is incident dementia, without an assigned food or Parkinson resting-tremor measure.

The smartphone accelerometer study compares rest and posture frequency features to distinguish Parkinson disease from essential tremor. The study uses diagnostic tasks without a raw-fig or dietary contrast.

This randomized-trial subsample compares eight weeks of active versus placebo transcranial pulsed electromagnetic-field treatment. The rest and postural hand recordings evaluate stimulation effects, with no food exposure.

Participants with Parkinson disease or essential tremor perform elbow pursuit-tracking tasks while an orthosis mechanically suppresses oscillation. The contrast evaluates a device during voluntary movement without fig intake.

The methods article describes recording and interpreting hand tremor using electrophysiologic and motion measures. Its diagnostic procedures do not compare a raw-fig exposure or a food-related tremor outcome.

The experiment measures mechanomyographic oscillations during a bilateral motor task in Parkinson patients without clinical tremor and healthy controls. It does not administer fig or assess a dietary resting-tremor response.

The neural-network study separates voluntary and involuntary components in hand movement signals from Parkinson and essential tremor recordings. The protocol includes supported rest positions, without a fig intake measure.

Three-dimensional motion capture and a force platform compare tremor under subthalamic stimulation and visual conditions. The Parkinson clinical experiment varies stimulation and vision without testing fig intake.

The retrospective comparison measures non-motor symptoms across essential tremor, Parkinson motor subtypes and healthy controls. Tremor classification defines diagnostic groups, with no fig exposure or food effect.

Mechanical oscillations and accelerometry are measured during a unilateral isometric task in Parkinson patients without clinical tremor and controls. These measurements do not test raw fig or food effects on rest tremor.

The experiment applies single-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation and measures Parkinson tremor rhythm and power through electromyography. The stimulation comparison supplies no fig exposure or dietary effect.

Phase-locked peripheral median-nerve stimulation is compared with spontaneous variation in hand rest tremor. Modulation depends on the phase and oscillation pattern, with no dietary exposure or fig contrast.
The imaging study relates cholinergic-relevant functional reactivity to differences in Parkinson tremor response to dopamine. The observed medication response does not evaluate raw-fig intake.

The study compares short-pulse and directional thalamic or posterior subthalamic stimulation in Parkinson disease and essential tremor. The contrast is between stimulation settings without a fig exposure.
The observational study compares Parkinson tremor with essential tremor during a specified hand posture. Diagnostic sensor findings do not measure fig consumption or food-linked clinical rest tremor.

This review summarizes clinical features, prevalence and classification of essential tremor accompanied by rest tremor. Its cited cohorts do not yield a raw-fig intervention or a fig-related estimate for Parkinson severity.

Simultaneous brain imaging and tremor recording relate fluctuating brain integration and arousal to spontaneous Parkinson rest-tremor fluctuations. There is no fig intake measurement or dietary contrast.

The systematic review and Bayesian analysis evaluate electrical, magnetic and light stimulation for Parkinson tremor. The compared exposures are stimulation modalities without a dietary fig intervention.
The feasibility study predicts Parkinson hand-tremor occurrence from EEG dynamics. The analysis tests signals and prediction performance without a dietary exposure or fig-related change.
The deep-brain stimulation study relates electrically activated tissue and fiber tracts to tremor suppression. Its tract-based therapeutic comparison supplies no raw-fig exposure.

The wearable-technology review treats eating and pouring drinks as task examples for kinetic tremor. The reviewed assessment techniques do not evaluate what foods are consumed or a fig effect on resting tremor.

This follow-up reports motor and non-motor outcomes after unilateral MRI-guided focused ultrasound thalamotomy for tremor-dominant Parkinson disease. Its tremor assessments compare surgery and follow-up without a fig exposure.

Inertial measurements compare tremor during walking, rest and re-emergent tremor in Parkinson disease. The study distinguishes motor conditions and does not measure fig intake or a food-related effect.

The double-blind Parkinson crossover compares a single dose of propranolol with placebo while measuring resting tremor and cognitive-load responses. The oral substance is a beta-blocker, with no fig intervention.

The classifier distinguishes subclinical resting-tremor signals from Parkinson, essential tremor and healthy recordings. The comparison uses motion data and machine learning, without measuring food intake or a fig effect.

The network analysis compares stimulation-associated tremor improvement and separately maps rest and action or postural items in Supplementary Figures S8 and S9. The compared exposures are procedures and connectivity, without raw-fig intake.

The diagnostic study compares neurofilament light from neuronally derived extracellular vesicles across Parkinson disease and essential tremor with resting tremor. The biomarker difference supplies no intake comparison.
The study evaluates a wrist-worn phase-tracking algorithm for Parkinson resting tremor. Its experimental signal and in-clinic device validation do not measure food intake or a raw-fig effect.

The structural imaging analysis compares subcortical anatomy across essential tremor and Parkinson disease with and without a tremor phenotype. It reports no fig dietary contrast or consumption-related resting-tremor change.

The study compares postural hand-tremor rhythmicity features in Parkinson and essential tremor. This diagnostic accelerometry contrast does not test food intake or a fig-related resting-tremor outcome.

The systematic review summarizes rest and action tremor prevalence and characteristics in multiple system atrophy. The disease comparison supplies no fig intervention or Parkinson dietary resting-tremor estimate.

The community KORA-Age study relates mild action tremor to cognition. Alcohol is included among participant variables. The analysis does not measure fig intake or treatment of Parkinson resting-tremor severity.
